title: Are LLM Performance Benchmarks Reliable? — Ashok Chandrasekar & Jason Kramberger, Google
talk_summary: Google engineers argue that most benchmark discrepancies come from the benchmark harness, not the system under test: Python GIL caps load, clients inflate latency, and dataset/temperature choices silently change results. They present inference-perf, a multi-process load generator with declarative configs, client-side observability, and a shared workload catalog to make benchmarks reproducible.

takeaways.technique: Instrument the harness, not just the system under test
takeaways.what_they_do: The load generator reports client-side metrics (planned vs actual execution time, achieved QPS) alongside server metrics so you can tell whether the harness itself failed to deliver the configured load.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you ask for 200 QPS and then you don't know whether it actually delivered it. It will just say I ran it these are the numbers
takeaways.numbers: Requested 200 QPS, single-process harness delivered 38 QPS on small machines and capped ~170 QPS on a bigger one; client-side thrashing inflated latency up to 58 seconds

takeaways.technique: Pin stochastic variables to match production
takeaways.what_they_do: They flag that a benchmark reporting 20% better throughput had set temperature to 0, making outputs deterministic and unrepresentative of real 0.7-temperature workloads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the benchmark harness were setting the model temperature to zero ... it was able to turn out a higher throughput than what you would normally see
takeaways.numbers: 20% better throughput claim traced to temperature=0 vs ~0.7

takeaways.what_they_do: They publish declarative workload configs (multi-turn, tree-of-thought, agentic code generation, batch summarization) in natural language plus tool-agnostic parameters so results are comparable across tools and runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a published set of some of these workloads and configuration ... tied to state-of-the-art inference workloads

takeaways.what_they_do: A user-defined declarative configuration captures all knobs (input/output length distributions, concurrency model, dataset sampling) so runs are reproducible across people and time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a userdefined declarative configuration uh that allows you to have clear reproducibility across runs
takeaways.numbers: Same ShareGPT dataset across two harnesses produced different input token counts due to different sampling/truncation

takeaways.technique: Multi-process load generation to escape single-thread limits
takeaways.what_they_do: A main process schedules requests by planned time and fans them across worker processes, avoiding Python GIL serialization and keeping overhead low at high concurrency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a load generator uh that solves the GIL problem in Python uh across multiple processes
takeaways.numbers: Sustained 5,000 QPS where single-process tools capped out
